title: The Concept of Cognitive Dissonance
text:
Cognitive dissonance describes the mental discomfort experienced by an individual who holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values; or is confronted by new information that conflicts with existing beliefs. This psychological state creates a motivational drive to reduce the internal inconsistency and restore cognitive equilibrium.

Individuals are motivated to reduce this dissonance through various means, such as altering one of the conflicting cognitions, adding new consonant beliefs to outweigh the discrepancy, or selectively ignoring evidence that contradicts their current belief system. The magnitude of the dissonance is typically proportional to the importance of the beliefs involved in the conflict.

Understanding this mechanism provides insight into human irrationality and self-justification processes. It explains why people often cling stubbornly to positions, even when overwhelming contradictory evidence exists.
